status_summary: Governmentwide Trusted Workforce 2.0 work continues with the DNI as Security Executive Agent: the Performance Accountability Council's FY2026 third-quarter report records the FBI as the first provider approved to use the new investigative standards (April), DCSA's retirement of legacy periodic reinvestigation products at the end of June, and continuous-vetting enrollment at 78 percent, while rating risk management as poor and noting slower investigation processing. GAO told a House Oversight subcommittee on 2026-02-24 that the reform's completion target had moved from the end of FY2026 to the end of FY2028. ODNI's August 2025 fact sheet kept NCSC and refocused it on clearance reform, counterintelligence threats and leak investigations, and Division F of Public Law 119-60 (signed 2025-12-18) includes a section on inactive security clearances (Sec. 6310). No move of the Security Services Directorate into ODNI, and no DNI action specifically enforcing the 48-hour reciprocity guidance, was found; neither the quarterly report nor the GAO statement mentions reciprocity.

End of the FY2026 third quarter covered by the Performance Accountability Council's personnel vetting report: FBI approved in April as first provider to use the new standards, DCSA retired legacy periodic reinvestigation products at the end of June, continuous-vetting enrollment 78 percent, and the Security Executive Agent named as DNI Jay Clayton (the report is undated; the date is the quarter's end).

title: Enforce Trusted Workforce 2.0 and reciprocity; elevate the Security Services Directorate
uncertainties: The quarterly report's publication date was not stated; its date here is the end of the covered quarter (an inference). Reciprocity timeliness, the 48-hour reciprocity guidance, NCSC and the Security Services Directorate are not mentioned in the quarterly report or the GAO statement, both of which were re-read on 2026-10-18. Section 6310 of Public Law 119-60, read on the Senate intelligence committee's copy, directs the DNI to review the feasibility of restoring eligibility for people separated up to five years and to assess continuous vetting of inactive clearances, with findings due within 120 days; it does not address reciprocity enforcement. Security Executive Agent directives and the Trusted Workforce 2.0 page are hosted on dni.gov, which could not be reached, so a DNI reciprocity directive issued since 2025 cannot be ruled out. Most of the governmentwide program predates 2025, so stage credit reflects continued implementation under the DNI as Security Executive Agent rather than the Mandate's specific enforcement steps. A search for a move of the Security Services Directorate found nothing, but internal ODNI reorganizations may not be public.
